c.tagline: Jamaica's pulsing capital, birthplace of reggae and Blue Mountain coffee.

taxi.fareNote: Use licensed JUTA taxis (red PP plates) and agree the fare before setting off, as most aren't metered. Shared 'route taxis' run fixed routes for a couple of dollars but aren't ideal for visitors with luggage; avoid unmarked cabs, especially at night.

emergency.note: Dial 119 for police and 110 for fire and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.New Kingston: Emancipation Park with its Redemption Song statue
hood_landmark.Liguanea: Hope Royal Botanical Gardens' lawns and zoo
hood_landmark.Half Way Tree: the landmark Half Way Tree Clock Tower crossroads
hood_landmark.Downtown Kingston: National Gallery of Jamaica on the waterfront
hood_landmark.Barbican & Cherry Gardens: upscale dining and shopping strip around Barbican Centre and Sovereign North

avoid.reason: Avoid inner-city garrison communities — Trench Town, Tivoli Gardens, Denham Town, August Town. Periodic states of emergency.

hood_desc: The uptown business and hotel hub along Knutsford Boulevard, home to most of the city's hotels, banks, embassies, restaurants, and the busiest bars and clubs; the standard and safest base for visitors.
A leafy, upscale residential district north of the centre near the University of the West Indies, quieter and green; suits travellers who want calm and are happy to taxi in and out.
St Andrew's bustling commercial core and transport interchange around the historic clock tower, with shopping plazas, markets, and street food; lively by day and the city's main crossroads.

The historic waterfront and old commercial core, home to the National Gallery of Jamaica, the harbourfront, Coronation Market, and the reggae heritage of nearby Trench Town; rich in sights but best explored by day with a guide or driver.
Upscale hillside residential neighbourhoods on the northern edge of the city, calm and green, and the gateway to the Blue Mountains and their coffee estates; quiet, scenic, and car-dependent.
lodging: ROK Hotel Kingston, Tapestry Collection by Hilton

water.note: Kingston's tap water is treated and safe to drink.

transit.hours: JUTC city buses run from roughly 5:00 AM to around 10:00-11:00 PM; shared route taxis fill the gaps but thin out and are best avoided after dark.
transit.note: The state-run Jamaica Urban Transit Company (JUTC) operates city buses across the Kingston Metropolitan Region, supplemented by shared 'route taxis' and minibuses on routes buses don't cover. There is no rail or metro. Licensed JUTA taxis and ride apps are the recommended way for visitors to get around, especially at night.
transit.pay: JUTC buses use a rechargeable Smarter Card (or exact cash on some routes); route taxis are paid in cash directly to the driver.

bus: Knutsford Express (intercity coach to Montego Bay, Ocho Rios and beyond)

transit.m: Licensed JUTA taxi to New Kingston (30-45 min)
JUTC bus toward downtown (cheaper but slow, daytime only)

tip.r: A 10% service charge is often added at restaurants; if it isn't, 10-15% is customary for good service.
